test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 28 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The value of acceleration due to gravity 'g' is _______

options.text: negative at the equator and positive at the poles
greater at the equator than at the poles
the same at the poles and equator
greater at the poles than at the equator

solution:
The correct answer is __**greater at the poles than at the equator**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The acceleration due to gravity (**g**) is not uniform across the Earth's surface due to its **non-spherical shape** and **rotational motion**.
 
• The Earth is an **oblate spheroid**, meaning it is flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator.
 
• At the poles, the distance between the Earth's center and the surface is **shorter** compared to the equator. Since gravity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, **g is greater at the poles**.
 
• The Earth's rotational motion creates a **centrifugal force**, which is maximum at the equator and reduces the net gravitational pull. This centrifugal force is negligible at the poles, resulting in a **higher value of g**.
 
• Mathematically, the relationship between gravity and distance can be expressed as **g ∝ 1/r²**, where r is the radius of the Earth at a given location.
 
• Thus, the combination of the Earth's shape and rotation explains why gravity is **greater at the poles** than at the equator.
